findings.text: follow-on: the new public TelemetryIndex.rollback method and the run() call to it are documented as necessary -- the run() docstring and the landed evidence fragment both say a lock error can leave an open transaction that must be discarded before the next tick -- but the call is not load-bearing for the reproduced path. The lock in the reproduced defect is raised by the resume lookup _consumed_whole_and_untouched, a SELECT issued before the pass's try block; under sqlite3's default isolation_level a SELECT opens no transaction, so there is nothing to roll back at that point. Demonstrated: removing the index.rollback() call from a scratch copy of the head telemetry_ingest.py leaves tests/test_telemetry_ingest.py green (19 passed, EXIT=0, independent-mutation-rollback.log), identical to head. The method is harmless and a reasonable defensive guard for a path that could leave a transaction open, but today no such path exists and no test exercises the rollback. Recorded so the rollback is not read as a proven requirement.

follow_ons.text: The landed evidence fragment asserts 'That statement sits outside the ingest pass's own try/except BaseException, which is why the failed pass left an artifact that needed to be rolled back explicitly'. The first clause is accurate (the resume lookup is a SELECT issued before the pass's try block); the second is not demonstrated, because a SELECT opens no transaction and removing index.rollback() leaves the locked-index test green (. independent-mutation-rollback.log). The fragment is the reviewed node's own landed record and is not this review's to edit, so no finding is raised against it; it is recorded so a reader does not take the rollback as a proven need.

item_verdicts.goal: The node's goal is that the standing ingest survive a locked index rather than ending its process on transient contention. The change does exactly that: run() wraps tick() in a try, and on a sqlite3.OperationalError whose message names a locked or busy file (the new _is_lock_error predicate) it discards the failed tick's transaction, keeps the fingerprints the tick began from, announces the failure on one flushed line, and ticks again. Every other OperationalError still propagates, shown by test_an_operational_error_that_is_not_a_lock_still_ends_the_process. A failed tick now counts as one of a finite iterations, so a bounded caller cannot spin on a lock that never clears. This is the code counterpart of section 5's 'Readings settled after the read-back' bullet, where the supervisor relaunches the ingest on exit: a transient lock no longer forces that restart.

justifications: independent review of run r-20261002T181215921664-srw-ingest-survives-a-locked-index, stored as a parsed record scoring all five dimensions in 0..20 -- goal_fidelity 18, evidence 16, scope_discipline 19, durability 18, fit 17 -- total 88, added_failure_count 0 with added_failure_ids [] derived from this review's own two arms of the reviewed run's declared three-file gate (the reviewed run was dispatched unarmed, so its own baseline_suite and after_suite are null): base arm gate-base.log (scratch tree $TMPDIR/arms/base, revision 175631f8: 84 passed, EXIT=0) and head arm gate-head.log (scratch tree $TMPDIR/arms/head, revision e95b68ad: 87 passed, EXIT=0); the head set adds three tests and removes none, so the delta is 0. The change reproduces independently: the ingest loop now catches SQLite's lock error, and the guarded behaviour was made to happen (a second connection holds BEGIN EXCLUSIVE) rather than read off a green suite. The node's negative control was reproduced in spirit and independently falsified: the reviewer's own mutation, making _is_lock_error always return False so a lock propagates, reddens test_a_locked_index_fails_one_tick_and_the_next_ingests_what_was_pending (1 failed, EXIT=1, independent-mutation.log). One finding: TelemetryIndex.rollback and its run() call are documented as needed, but removing the call leaves the suite green (independent-mutation-rollback.log, 19 passed, EXIT=0), so the rollback is defensive rather than load-bearing for the reproduced path, and the landed evidence fragment's claim that the failed pass left an artifact needing explicit rollback was not reproducible. Scope is clean (exactly the declared paths, nothing outside), durability is sound (conventional commits with bodies, no AI attribution, evidence fragment committed, tree clean, three tests added).
